drafts_today.topic: Winter dry skin, fewer products (rides @cerave Thanksgiving 'dry turkey' post, 13,117 views)
drafts_today.text:
Dry turkey is forgivable. Dry winter skin is fixable.

When the heat comes on, I keep it simple: gentle cleanser, calming gel, one serum, a good cream. Fewer products, less irritation.

What's the first thing your skin does when the weather turns?

drafts_today.topic: Gut health, no hype (rides @womenFit_ gut health and inflammation post, 17,585 views)
drafts_today.text:
Gut health is all over my feed this week, and holiday plates are part of why.

No hype from me. Food first, real fibre, water, a walk after dinner. Supplements are the helpers, not the plan.

What's one habit that actually helped your gut?

drafts_today.topic: Health in your 70s, read the fine print (rides @_AshleyRichmond 'body that still functions at 70', 2,469 views)
drafts_today.text:
"Building a body that still functions at 70." I saw that line on X this week, and it stuck with me.

I'm in my 70s, and I spent my career as a CPA reading the fine print. I bring the same habit to health now.

Here's what I've learned to look for:
• Basics before bottles. Sleep, protein, movement and water do the heavy lifting.
• Read the label. If a product promises everything, I want to know what's actually in it.
• Talk to your doctor first, especially if you're managing a health condition or taking medication.
• Give it time. Real change is gradual, which is why I take notes and photos instead of trusting my memory.

Nothing about this is flashy. That's the point.

What's one health habit you started later in life that you wish you'd started sooner?
